title: Introduction and learning objectives
groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture on cancer causation and states what students should learn.

title: Mutation-driven cancer evolution and susceptibility
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations accumulate and enable cancer to evolve under conditions that favour susceptible cells.

title: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures contribute to cancer rather than cancer being attributable simply to genetics or chance.

title: Infectious causes of cancer
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma developing the argument through a detailed example.

title: Mechanisms of environmental DNA damage
groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations, showing how their effects depend on processing within the body.

title: Tumour initiation and promotion
groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish initiating mutations from the promotional conditions that allow mutated cells to proliferate into tumours.

title: Developmental and tissue specificity of carcinogens
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how susceptibility to carcinogens depends on the biological context of exposure and consolidate that principle within the preceding account of carcinogenesis.

title: Identifying carcinogenic exposures in human cancers
groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how evidence collected from human cancers and populations can connect particular exposures with cancer development.

title: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
groupedBecause: These subtopics examine controlled experimental tests of carcinogenic potential and why their results cannot fully predict cancer risk in humans.

title: Concluding summary and risk–benefit decisions
groupedBecause: The closing summarises the lecture's conclusions and frames everyday exposure decisions as a balance between risks and benefits.
